keyFindings.description: The rewritten rule exempts uvx from the coordinate half, and that exemption is false: 'uvx <name>@<version> and go run <module>@<version> take the coordinate directly ... there the version is the half left to you' (identically at docs/kubernetes.md:233-235). uv resolves the typed token as the PyPI project, not as a command: `uvx --help` documents `--from <FROM>  Use the given package to provide the command`, and driven in this role container, `uvx pyyaml@6.0.2 --version` printed 'Installed 1 package in 23ms' then 'Package `pyyaml` does not provide any executables.' -- uv installed the project named by the token and only then looked for an executable of that name. So a worker who knows a Python tool's command name and types `uvx <command>@<version>`, which is exactly what the form at tools.md:47 invites, installs whatever PyPI project owns that name and runs its entry points and build hooks inside the role container. That is the same failure class as `bunx biome` -> 0.3.3, in the very page written against it, and the page tells the reader this half is safe. The form `uvx --from <package>@<version> <binary>` appears nowhere, so a Python tool whose script differs from its distribution also has no documented form at all. Round 1 raised this gap and the rewrite hardened the wrong way.

The coordinate check the rule prescribes rests on fields the publisher controls, and the claim made for it is false as a general rule: 'Check it once, before the tool's first use ... npm view <name> version description repository.url homepage. The real package's answer names the project's own repository and site; the squatter's names neither' (same at docs/kubernetes.md:202-206, transcripts at tools.md:73-82 and docs/kubernetes.md:208-217). npm serves `repository` and `homepage` straight from the publisher's own package.json and verifies neither against the repository they name, so a squatter closes this check by copying two strings; a legitimate package that omits `homepage` reads as a squat. The generalisation is drawn from one observation of one squatter. It is the single verification step the page tells a worker to perform before first use, so the false guarantee is the defect, not the check's existence.

Round 1's 'a role cannot fetch a compiled client for itself' overstatement was corrected in the paragraph the finding cited and in tools.md, and survives in two further copies, one of them the published site. docs/kubernetes.md:155: 'The image answers the tools a non-root container can never fetch for itself', fifteen lines above the corrected paragraph at :170-175 and the extraction row at :182 that both contradict it. docs/site/src/content/docs/legion/running-legion.md:187-188: 'the client tools a role's own work needs (psql, redis-cli, sqlite3, nc, dig), which an unprivileged container could not install for itself'. Both need the corrected bar: apt cannot install into a system prefix, and Legion rules extraction out by ruling.

The ground now given for the prohibition forbids the step the same page prescribes. tools.md:37-43 and docs/kubernetes.md:170-175 say 'installing a tool for a role is the withheld operator-setup capability'; that row reads 'installs or configures its own dependencies in the pod: Legion owns its dependencies' (packages/daemon/internal/capabilities/capabilities.go:100, ruling dispatch://LEGION-200). uvx, bunx --package and go run install dependencies in the pod too, onto the very caches docs/kubernetes.md:180 lists (UV_CACHE_DIR, BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR, GOCACHE, GOMODCACHE), so as written the ruling rules out the documented step as well, and a worker is given no line between the two. The plan drew one (the container's own filesystem versus the issue's disk, .legion/INFRA-221/plan.json gapAnalysis F10) and it is not the line shipped. The same sentence carried into docs/solutions/testing/...-LEGION-748.md:55-60 declares that learning's $HOME/.local installs withheld 'in any case'; of the tools it recorded, PyYAML survives through uv but shellcheck is left with no route but an image change, so a documented step was removed from a standing learning without a replacement.

The like-for-like re-measurement is right and verified, but the sentence still hangs off the wrong number: 'The five client tools ... cost 7.9 MiB of that total', where 'that total' is the 22-layer, 1007 MiB sha-ff33c8c9fb1b build named at :249-251, while the pair that follows is 24 layers, 1026.9 against 1019.0 MiB. Three totals for 'the image' in four sentences, and the subtraction uses none of the first. Round 1 opened this thread; the baseline half was fixed and this half was not.

The annotation's shape is not the one this repository uses for superseding a learning: it opens `*2026-10-24:*` where the convention elsewhere is a bolded 'Superseded <date> (<KEY>):' lead naming the issue that superseded it (rebasing-a-branch-...md:29, template-names-...md:111, shell-command-gates-...md:107,132, shared-main-repo-hazards-...md:75; the rule in skills/legion-retro/SKILL.md:86-88,99-105). Not blocking; worth one line while the file is open.

The duplicated runner prose grew rather than shrank: twinned near-identical lines between docs/kubernetes.md's subsection and skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md went from 29 at afb6d688 to 46 at this head, with two blocks now byte-identical (docs/kubernetes.md:208-217 == tools.md:73-82, the npm view transcript; docs/kubernetes.md:222-229 == tools.md:87-94, the bunx transcript), and the two copies have already drifted on what uvx prints (docs/kubernetes.md:190-191 collapses the refusal into one quoted string and loses the `cause:` line that tools.md:49-50 keeps; the real output is two lines, as tools.md has it). Both copies had to take the same two rewrites by hand this round. It stays the round's one Fast-follow, since duplication and wording cleanup are what that line is for, but it is the second round it has cost.
